edits.value_json: The ordinary present-day meaning is ‘four.’ A middle Western Zhou bronze inscription is reported in a four-horse context, but the available transcription does not verify whether the numeral is 四 or 亖. The evidence does not establish the earliest use or how 四 originated.

四 means “four.” Its present structure is an enclosing 囗 around inner 儿-form strokes. Early forms are described as marks used directly for “four”; the counting-rod explanation and separate borrowing proposals involving 呬 (breath) and 泗 (nasal discharge) remain disputed.
